process_area.title: Green Fleet Performance, Compliance, Safety & Analytics

value_stream.name: Green Fleet Transition, Electric Vehicle (EV) Fleet Operations & Sustainable Transportation

fields.Participants: Fleet (VS-06), Fuel (VS-61), Charging Ops (W5473), Finance (VS-17.4), External assurance (VS-21)
fields.Trigger: Baseline established (W5465); monthly/quarterly/annual ESG reporting cycle

workflows.name: Fleet GHG Emissions Measurement, MRV & Scope 1 Reduction Reporting

Automation Opportunity: - Fuel-card/charging → carbon-accounting auto-posting; EF library with auto-refresh; reduction-attribution analytics; audit-ready evidence pack generation.
Controls: - CTL-808 (ensure controlled execution — Green Fleet Performance, Compliance, Safety & Analytics (PA-192.3).)
- operational: documented GHG Protocol methodology; conservative-EF policy; external assurance for public disclosure.
Cross-references: - links to VS-25 (ESG/MRV W694/W1334), VS-61 (fuel), VS-17 (financial reconciliation), VS-21 (assurance), W5465 (baseline/target), W5473/W5486 (charging data), W5478 (alt-fuel EF), W5485 (3PL data), W5488 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data-gap risk**: incomplete 3PL or telematics data understates Scope 1 and overstates reductions; mitigated by the 3PL green-data clause (W5485) and conservative top-down estimation until complete.

- **Greenwashing-disclosure risk**: overstated reductions in assured ESG disclosure create regulatory/reputational exposure (SEC/VS-173, VS-25); mitigated by conservative EFs, documented methodology, and external assurance.
- **EF-staleness risk**: outdated grid EFs mis-state the electricity Scope 2 benefit; mitigated by periodic EF refresh to current PH/IEA values.
System Touchpoints: - ESG data platform (VS-25); fuel/fleet cost (VS-61); charging/billing (W5473/W5486); carbon-accounting/MRV module; financial records (VS-17); assurance (VS-21).
Time Estimate: - Automated data aggregation monthly; ~1–2 weeks/annual assured reporting cycle.

steps.activity: Aggregate activity data per GHG Protocol Scope 1: diesel/gasoline litres (VS-61), biodiesel/LNG/CNG (W5478), and the residual liquid-fuel share of the owned fleet; capture electricity kWh for EV charging separately (Scope 2, per W5479 renewable-share).

Apply emission factors (Philippine/IEA grid EF for electricity; fuel-specific EF for liquids; certified lifecycle EF for biodiesel per W5478) consistently with the corporate GHG inventory methodology.
Compute actual tCO₂e vs the decarbonization target (W5465) and the ex-ante baseline (W5471); attribute reductions to electrification, alt-fuel, eco-driving (W5476), and route redesign (W5472).
Report into the corporate ESG/Scope-1 disclosure (VS-25 W694/W1334) and any voluntary framework (GHG Protocol, TCFD/ISSB, CDP); support external assurance (VS-21).
Maintain MRV evidence (activity-data records, EF sourcing, calculations) audit-ready; reconcile to the fuel/energy financial records (VS-61/VS-17).

fields.Frequency: Per inspection cycle; per franchise renewal; per reporting requirement
fields.Trigger: EV/alt-fuel vehicles in service; annual inspection/franchise cycle; regulatory reporting
fields.Volume: Per green-fleet vehicle and per for-hire/goods vehicle franchise

workflows.name: DOE / LTO / LTFRB Green-Fleet Compliance, EV Inspection & Franchise Reporting

Automation Opportunity: - Compliance-calendar expiry alerts (VS-166); inspection-scheduling automation; regulatory-reporting templating and evidence repository.
Controls: - CTL-808 (ensure controlled execution — Green Fleet Performance, Compliance, Safety & Analytics (PA-192.3).)
- operational: LTO/LTFRB/DOE permit/registration verification with statutory reporting compliance; inspection-before-renewal sequencing; central evidence repository.
Cross-references: - links to VS-166 (license portfolio), VS-22/VS-100 (compliance/legal), VS-06 (fleet), VS-06.2 (inspection/PM), VS-25 (ESG), W5470 (EVIDA incentives/registration), W5475/W5480 (SoH/PM)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Franchise-lapse risk**: a lapsed LTFRB franchise halts for-hire/goods operations and incurs penalties; mitigated by the central compliance calendar (VS-166).
- **Inspection-failure risk**: an EV failing inspection (e.g., HV/battery integrity) is grounded; mitigated by the SoH/PM programs (W5475/W5480) ahead of inspection.

- **EVIDA-reporting-obligation risk**: an unmet DOE/EVIDA data/reporting obligation attracts regulatory attention and forfeits incentive eligibility; mitigated by ongoing monitoring (W5470 step 5) and this workflow.
System Touchpoints: - Compliance/portfolio register (VS-166); fleet asset register (VS-06); legal (VS-100); ESG (VS-25); maintenance inspection (VS-06.2).

steps.activity: Maintain EV/alt-fuel vehicle registrations with the LTO under the EV-specific path (W5470) and arrange annual motor-vehicle inspection (private inspection center / LTO) covering EV-specific items (battery/HV integrity where inspected).
For goods/for-hire vehicles and the rental fleet (VS-162), maintain LTFRB franchise/CPC compliance and any EV-franchise incentives/requirements under EVIDA IRR.
Report to the DOE/EVIDA Implementing Body any fleet-EV-share or program data called for under the EVIDA IRR and EV roadmap, and respond to DOE/LTO data calls.
Coordinate any LGU EV-parking/charging ordinances (under RA 11697 building/parking provisions) at new/remodel sites (VS-37/VS-109), ensuring compliance in the license portfolio (VS-166).
Maintain the green-fleet compliance evidence repository (LTO inspection, LTFRB franchise, DOE reporting, LGU EV compliance) for audit and VS-21.

workflows.name: EV & Alt-Fuel Fleet Safety — High-Voltage, Battery Fire & DOLE-OSH Program

Automation Opportunity: - Incident-reporting workflow with auto-routing to DOLE/BFP where reportable; HV-work-permit/LOTO enforcement in the CMMS; thermal-event telemetry auto-alerting (W5475/W5480).
Controls: - CTL-808 (ensure controlled execution — Green Fleet Performance, Compliance, Safety & Analytics (PA-192.3).)
- operational: HV-work-permit/LOTO mandatory; lithium-fire-appropriate suppression; qualified-only HV work; reportable-incident DOLE/BFP notification.
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE/incident), VS-138 (facilities/BFP), VS-19.4 (training), VS-22 (DOLE/BFP reporting), W5468 (BFP-compliant siting), W5480 (HV-safe PM/towing), W5484 (HV-qualification training)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lithium-battery-fire risk**: a thermal-runaway fire is intense, toxic, and re-igniting, and water suppression is contraindicated; mitigated by appropriate suppression (e.g., specialized agents, containment), separation, and trained response.
- **HV-shock risk**: untrained contact with HV systems is lethal; mitigated by HV-work-permit and LOTO discipline, qualified-only work (W5480), and training.
- **Unprepared-first-responder risk**: municipal responders unfamiliar with EV incidents respond unsafely; mitigated by coordination/drills and OEM emergency-response guides onboard vehicles.
System Touchpoints: - HSE/incident management (VS-24); facilities/Fire Code (VS-138); maintenance (W5480); L&D/competency (VS-19.4); BFP/DOLE reporting (VS-22).
Time Estimate: - Program establishment ~weeks; per-event investigation ~hours–days; drills absorbed into VS-24.

steps.activity: Establish the EV/alt-fuel fleet safety program under DOLE-OSH (RA 11058) and BFP Fire Code: HV-work permits, LOTO/energy-isolation for HV systems, battery-fire response, and first-responder protocols.

Site the charging/alt-fuel infrastructure with BFP-compliant separation, fire-detection/suppression appropriate to lithium-battery fires (not water), ventilation, and emergency shut-off (links W5468).
Train drivers, technicians, and first-responders (links W5484) on HV safety, battery-fire response, and towing/recovery (W5480); maintain competency records.
Investigate every HV/thermal/fire event to root cause (links VS-24 incident investigation), with corrective/preventive action; report serious incidents to DOLE/BFP per OSH/Fire-Code requirements.
Maintain emergency-response readiness (drills, equipment, mutual-aid with BFP/LGU) and feed systemic issues into the recall path and the OEM/battery vendor (W5467/W5480).

fields.Trigger: EV/alt-fuel vehicles entering service; new hires/drivers/technicians; recurring certification

workflows.name: Green Fleet Driver & Technician Training, Certification & Behavior Incentive Program

Automation Opportunity: - Competency-gated vehicle/work assignment; eco-score-driven coaching-task assignment; certification-expiry alerts (links VS-166 pattern).
Controls: - CTL-808 (ensure controlled execution — Green Fleet Performance, Compliance, Safety & Analytics (PA-192.3).)
- operational: DOLE-OSH HV-qualification compliance with certification/competency evidence; no EV/HV assignment without valid certification; re-certification cadence.
Cross-references: - links to VS-19.4 (L&D/competency), VS-124 (enablement/coaching), VS-24 (HSE), W5476 (eco-driving/incentives), W5480 (HV-safe maintenance), W5483 (HV-safety training)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Uncertified-assignment risk**: a driver/technician assigned to EV/HV work without valid certification creates safety and compliance exposure; mitigated by competency-gated assignment.
- **Range-erosion-from-poor-driving risk**: untrained drivers erode the TCO case (W5476); mitigated by mandatory eco-driving training and incentives.
System Touchpoints: - L&D/HR system (VS-19.4); fleet/telematics eco-scores (W5476); HSE/competency (VS-24); maintenance (W5480); enablement (VS-124).
Time Estimate: - Per onboarding course ~hours; recurring re-certification ~annually; absorbed into VS-19.4/L&D.

steps.activity: Deliver EV/alt-fuel driver training: eco-driving for range (links W5476), charging discipline, HV-safety basics, emergency response, and towing/strand protocol; certify before EV assignment.
Deliver EV-specific maintenance technician training and HV-qualification (per OEM + DOLE-OSH) certifying safe HV-work (links W5480/W5483); re-certify periodically.
Operate the eco-driving incentive program (rewards/ recognition for top kWh/km and L/100km performers per W5476) and coach under-performers (links VS-124).
Maintain competency/certification records in the L&D/HR system (VS-19.4) and gate vehicle/HV-work assignment on valid certification (links W5480/W5483).
Refresh content on regulatory change, OEM updates, new drivetrains, and lessons learned from incidents (W5483) and analytics (W5488).

fields.Trigger: 3PL/ carrier contracting (VS-56/VS-110); RFP; annual carrier review
fields.Volume: ~80% of the outbound-distribution fleet is third-party (VS-06); plus last-mile (VS-56)

workflows.name: Third-Party / 3PL Carrier Green-Fleet Requirements, Contract Clauses & Scorecard

Automation Opportunity: - Carrier-data ingestion into the MRV; automated green-scorecard; contract-clause library and compliance tracking.
Controls: - CTL-808 (ensure controlled execution — Green Fleet Performance, Compliance, Safety & Analytics (PA-192.3).)
- operational: carrier TPRM with emissions-data evidence; phased green expectations; material-claim attestation requirement; scorecard-in-allocation policy.
Cross-references: - links to VS-110 (freight/carrier), VS-56 (3PL/last-mile), VS-161 (TPRM), VS-100 (contract/legal), VS-25 (ESG), W5481 (MRV), W5488 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **3PL-data-withholding risk**: carriers decline to share emissions/alt-fuel data, leaving the 80% outsourced share unmeasured; mitigated by contract clauses and allocation leverage.
- **Greenwashing-by-carrier risk**: a carrier overstates its green performance; mitigated by evidence requirements, third-party attestation for material claims, and TPRM monitoring.
- **Capacity-flight risk**: overly stringent green requirements drive carriers away in a tight PH freight market; mitigated by phased expectations and development support.
System Touchpoints: - Freight procurement/carrier (VS-110); 3PL/last-mile (VS-56); TPRM (VS-161); MRV/carbon (W5481); contract/legal (VS-100); ESG (VS-25).
Time Estimate: - Per RFP/contract cycle; ~quarterly scorecard absorbed into VS-110.

steps.activity: Define BuildRight's green-fleet requirements for carriers/3PLs: fleet-age/emissions standards, alt-fuel/EV-share expectations over the contract term, driver-behavior/telematics data sharing, and MRV data provision (links W5481).
Embed the green-fleet clauses in carrier/3PL contracts (links VS-110/VS-56/VS-161): emission targets, data-provision obligations, preferred-lane/EV assignment, and remedies for non-performance.
Collect carrier emissions/alt-fuel data (litres, kWh, tCO₂e per BuildRight-attributed tonne-km) into the MRV (W5481); apply TPRM monitoring (VS-161).
Score carriers on a green-fleet scorecard (emissions performance, alt-fuel/EV adoption progress, data quality, incidents) alongside the existing carrier scorecard (VS-110).
Use the scorecard in carrier allocation and renewal decisions; recognize/develop leading carriers and remediate or exit poor performers (links VS-110 W3515 freight-audit/contract).

fields.Frequency: Per billing cycle; monthly cost allocation
fields.Trigger: Charging sessions (W5473); electricity billing; reimbursement cycle
fields.Volume: Per fleet-charging session + any off-site/home/depot-charging reimbursement

workflows.name: EV Charging Billing, Electricity Cost Allocation, Reimbursement & Home-Charge Policy

Automation Opportunity: - Session→cost-center auto-allocation; session-vs-utility reconciliation with leakage alerting; reimbursement-claim workflow with evidence/cap enforcement.
Controls: - CTL-808 (ensure controlled execution — Green Fleet Performance, Compliance, Safety & Analytics (PA-192.3).)
- operational: reimbursement cap and evidence policy; documented cross-entity allocation keys.
Cross-references: - links to VS-120 (energy/utility), VS-61 (fleet cost), VS-158 (cost accounting), VS-17 (GL), VS-79 (tax), VS-72 (intercompany), W5473 (sessions), W5469 (TCO), W5479 (renewable-share)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cost-leakage risk**: un-allocated or un-billed charging electricity understates fleet cost and distorts TCO; mitigated by session-vs-utility reconciliation.
- **Reimbursement-fraud risk**: fabricated/inflated home-charge claims; mitigated by evidence requirements, caps, and audit.
- **Cross-entity-allocation risk**: mis-allocating charging cost across the 5 entities distorts entity P&L; mitigated by documented allocation keys (VS-72).
System Touchpoints: - Charging/billing (W5473/VS-163); energy/utility (VS-120); fleet cost (VS-61); cost accounting (VS-158); finance/GL (VS-17); tax (VS-79); intercompany (VS-72).
Time Estimate: - Automated allocation once configured; ~monthly reconciliation hours.

steps.activity: Allocate depot/site charging electricity cost to the fleet cost center per vehicle/session using session logs (W5473): kWh × tariff, including demand-charge apportionment and renewable-share (W5479).

Where drivers charge off-site (depot of a 3PL, public network, or home for take-home vehicles), define and operate the reimbursement policy: evidence (session receipt), rate, cap, and tax/RA-10173 handling.
Reconcile utility electricity bills (VS-120) to the session-log total to detect leakage (un-billed sessions, metering gaps) and recover/refund.
Feed accurate per-vehicle electricity cost into the TCO model (W5469) and the freight/fleet cost accounting (VS-158/VS-61).
Maintain VAT/treatment compliance on electricity and any reimbursement (links VS-79) and cost-allocation governance across entities (VS-72).

workflows.name: EV Battery Second-Life, End-of-Life Recycling & RA 11898 EPR Linkage

Automation Opportunity: - Battery-passport/traceability ledger; SoH-threshold auto-trigger of disposition workflow; accredited-TSD matching and manifest (links VS-114).
Controls: - CTL-808 (ensure controlled execution — Green Fleet Performance, Compliance, Safety & Analytics (PA-192.3).)
- operational: DENR-accredited TSD/RA 6969 manifest with traceability/EPR evidence and recycler/TSD TPRM; documented disposition decision framework; chain-of-custody mandatory.
Cross-references: - links to VS-06.2/VS-138 (maintenance/CMMS), VS-108 (second-life storage), VS-179 (EPR), VS-114/VS-187 (hazmat TSD), VS-35 (asset disposal), VS-25 (ESG), W5467 (procurement/take-back), W5475 (SoH/threshold)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Improper-disposal risk**: landfilling or informal recycling of lithium batteries breaches RA 6969/RA 11898 and creates fire/environmental liability; mitigated by accredited-TSD routing and chain-of-custody.
- **Orphan-chemistry risk**: a battery chemistry with no local recycler strands end-of-life; mitigated by chemistry-aware procurement (W5467) and OEM take-back terms.
- **Value-leakage risk**: forgoing second-life value where viable; mitigated by the second-life economics assessment (step 1–2).
System Touchpoints: - Battery lifecycle/passport (W5475); maintenance/CMMS (VS-06.2/VS-138); solar/storage (VS-108); EPR/ESG (VS-179/VS-25); DG/hazmat TSD (VS-114/VS-187); asset disposal (VS-35).
Time Estimate: - Per battery disposition decision ~hours–days; chain-of-custody absorbed.

steps.activity: At the degradation threshold (W5475), decide per battery: second-life reuse (stationary storage at a BuildRight site — links VS-108), refurbishment, or end-of-life recycling, based on SoH and economics.
For second-life, qualify the application (stationary storage capacity, BMS re-commissioning, safety), integrate with the solar/storage program (VS-108), and account for the residual value.
For end-of-life, route to an OEM take-back program or a DENR-accredited hazardous-waste transporter/TSD (RA 6969) and recycler capable of lithium-battery processing (links VS-187/VS-114).
Maintain battery traceability/passport (chemistry, SoH history, disposition, chain-of-custody to recycler) for ESG/EPR evidence and warranty (W5467/W5475).
Align with RA 11898 (EPR Act) obligations on e-waste/extended producer responsibility (links VS-179) and report battery diversion/recycling in ESG disclosure (VS-25).

fields.Trigger: Program live; monthly/quarterly performance review; annual strategy (W5465)

workflows.name: Green Fleet Performance Analytics, Decarbonization Tracking & Continuous Improvement

Automation Opportunity: - Unified green-fleet dashboard with anomaly alerting; benefit-realization auto-variance analysis; exception-based root-cause task generation; OpEx/process-mining integration (VS-133).
Controls: - CTL-808 (ensure controlled execution — Green Fleet Performance, Compliance, Safety & Analytics (PA-192.3).)
- operational: documented top-KPI set; exception-based review cadence.
Cross-references: - links to VS-28 (analytics/BI), VS-25 (ESG), VS-133 (OpEx/CI), VS-06 (fleet/telematics), VS-17.4/VS-158 (finance/cost), VS-40/VS-112 (capital/PMO), VS-36 (board), W5465 (strategy), W5469/W5471 (TCO/capital/benefit), W5481 (MRV)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Metric-gaming risk**: drivers/carriers game eco-scores or fallback-usage reporting; mitigated by data-quality controls and telematics integrity.

- **Benefit-shortfall-invisibility risk**: modeled savings silently fail to materialize without tracking; mitigated by the benefit-realization tracker vs ex-ante (W5471) and the VS-40/VS-112 post-investment review (W5487).
- **Analysis-paralysis risk**: rich telematics data overwhelms finite fleet/CI capacity; mitigated by a focused top-KPI set and exception-based review.
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (VS-28); ESG data (VS-25); OpEx/process-mining (VS-133); fleet/telematics (VS-06); finance/cost (VS-17.4/VS-158); capital/benefit tracking (VS-40/VS-112).
Time Estimate: - Automated dashboard; ~hours/week analyst; quarterly/annual review cycles.

steps.activity: Maintain the green-fleet performance dashboard: tCO₂e vs target (W5481), kWh/km & L/100km, eco-driving scores (W5476), charger uptime (W5474), fallback-usage (W5477), renewable-share (W5479), and cost/run vs TCO case (W5469).
Track benefit-realization vs the ex-ante business case (W5471): emissions reduction, energy/fuel cost savings, maintenance savings, and incentive realization; investigate variances.
Identify under-performing vehicles/lanes/sites/drivers and run root-cause (OpEx/VS-133): e.g., a site with high fallback-usage, a vehicle with abnormal degradation, a charger with low uptime.
Drive continuous improvement (links VS-133): route/charging-schedule tweaks, driver coaching, infrastructure additions, procurement-spec updates (W5467), and contract-clause refinement (W5485).
Report program performance into the ESG/decarbonization governance (VS-25/VS-36 board) and feed the annual strategy refresh (W5465) and capital governance (W5471).
